title: Lockboxes
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: The Airbnb summer. Key-safes on every door in the backgrounds. Tourist Season lasts three months. This is one daily of thirty.

panels.composition: Main street, July. WOOD walking BARNABY II. Every door in the background has a small gray lockbox on the knob. Every window has a laminated card. Not one face he knows.

image.prompt: a small coastal main street in July with a thin man walking a three-legged dog past a row of houses that each have a small gray key lockbox on the doorknob and a laminated card in the window, strangers with roller bags, clean ink with a light wash
image.notes: Lockboxes on every door. The strip's only comment is their presence.

panels.composition: One lockbox. A four-digit dial. A house he's drawn since 1997 — Chloe's parents' house. A card in the window: CHECK-IN 3PM.

image.prompt: close-up of a gray key lockbox on the front door of an old wooden house with a laminated check-in card in the window beside it
image.notes: Chloe's parents' house. Sold, rented, unremarked. Letter after: CHECK-IN 3PM.

panels.composition: Wood stopped. The pup pulling. Wood looking at the door for one panel longer than a stranger would.

image.prompt: a thin man stopped on a sidewalk looking at a house door while a three-legged dog pulls at the leash, no words

panels.composition: Walking on. A family with roller bags going up the walk behind him, punching the code. The strip draws them kindly. It's their house till Sunday.

characters.pose: a family with roller bags at the door

image.prompt: a thin man and a three-legged dog walking away as a family with roller bags climbs the walk of an old house behind him and opens a key lockbox, drawn kindly, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: dailies: ink and one tone. Sundays: gray-green, fog, rust, bruised dusk

notes: Chloe's parents' house, a rental now. The strip stops one panel longer than a stranger would.
